items.title: NVIDIA expands robot security stack, bets on "physical AI"
items.summary: Ars Technica reported that Nvidia is advancing a full-stack security solution for physical AI such as robots: Halos for autonomous driving will be launched in 2025 and expanded to robots (Halos for Robotics) in June 2026, including the IGX Thor computing module with an independent security processor, the Halos operating system that continuously monitors hardware and software libraries, the Holoscan Sensor Bridge, and simulation testing and inspection laboratories. Amit Goel, head of Nvidia's robotics ecosystem and edge computing, said that as models and hardware mature, security will become the next bottleneck; the article also mentioned that Jensen Huang previously stated that the annual revenue of the physical AI business has reached nearly 10 billion US dollars.
items.comment: It is worth noting that safety certification and tool chains may become key variables in the large-scale deployment of robots, not just the model capabilities themselves.

items.title: Microsoft releases Nvidia chip AI PC and Windows 11 revision
items.summary: Microsoft announced Surface Laptop Ultra and Surface RTX Spark Dev Box at its first offline launch event in two years. Both use NVIDIA RTX Spark SoC and focus on running AI models and agents locally. The starting prices are approximately US$2,599 and US$5,999 respectively, and will be shipped from October 16. Windows 11 synchronized update: Copilot is changed to three tabs: Home / Code / Autopilot, and the “Execution Containers” sandbox function for AI agents is introduced, which is said to be available to all Windows 11 users. Dell also announced details of the XPS 16 Creator Edition.
items.comment: It may mean that PC manufacturers are considering "local inference computing power" as a new selling point, but the price threshold and the actual benefits of local models still need to be verified.

items.title: ChatGPT launches Intelligent UI to generate interactive visual answers using GPT-6
items.summary: OpenAI has launched a new interface called Intelligent UI for ChatGPT. GPT-6 generates interactive visual elements such as charts, buttons, and calculators to answer questions. Pro, Plus, Business, and Enterprise users will go first, and free and Go grades will follow on a day-to-day basis; users can lower the proportion of visual elements. According to WIRED’s hands-on experience, when you ask for a schematic diagram from ChatGPT, you can get an anatomical diagram with clickable parts, a calculator with draggable sliders, etc., but not every answer will be accompanied by a picture.
items.comment: It is worth noting that “generative interfaces” may change the default interaction form of chatbots and also bring new issues of design consistency.

items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 released: Price aligned with GPT-6 Luna, but the tokenizer is more "expensive"
items.summary: Simon Willison introduced Anthropic's newly released fast and low-priced model Claude Haiku 5.5 in his blog: The pricing is the same as GPT-6 Luna within 100,000 tokens (input $0.10/output $0.50 per million tokens), and rises to $0.50/2.50 after exceeding 100,000 tokens. He used his Claude Token Counter to measure that the token consumed by the same long prompt word on Haiku 5.5 is about 1.25 times that of Haiku 4.5, which is equivalent to an implicit price increase. At the same time, Anthropic halved the cache read price of Sonnet 5.5 and issued monthly API quotas to Max/Team subscribers.
items.comment: From the author's point of view, the price comparison is based on his personal tool measurement, and the actual cost needs to be verified based on his own load.

items.title: Liquid AI open sourced two end-side decision-making models, d1-3B and d1-omni-600M
items.summary: Liquid AI released two open source weight models from its d1 decision model family on Hugging Face: d1-3B and the experimental d1-omni-600M. Officially, d1-3B scored 48.57 on Decision Index 0.2.1, which is better than all 4B/9B models and the 35B-A3B Decider; it supports text and image input, responds to a single question in about 16 milliseconds on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor, and inherits the visual capabilities of the LFM2.5-VL-3B backbone. d1-omni-600M supports text with images or text with audio. Both do not generate token-by-token, but give answers in a single forward pass.
items.comment: It is worth paying attention to the low-latency advantage of the non-generative route of "decision model" on edge devices, but the benchmark and device performance still need to be reproduced by a third party.

items.title: Technical practice: Use ML Intern agents to train small models that can run on the CPU
items.summary: The Hugging Face blogger wrote an article to record his personal practice: Due to the lack of a small-sized Qwen-Image 2.1 prompt word rewriter, he used the ML Intern agent in HuggingChat to train a 0.8B version that can run on the CPU. According to his description, the effective output rate is 99.7%, using about a quarter of the tokens of the teacher model, and the entire project (including 8797 pieces of annotated data) cost 16 US$; five additional models have since been completed and released in a similar manner. The article shares the key points of the budget cap, baseline comparison, smoke test and other prompt words. The prompt words have been published on GitHub.
items.comment: The author's personal technical practice records, cost and effect figures have not been verified by third parties.

items.title: Open source project nanoMuse: a personal agent benchmarking against Meta Muse
items.summary: Papers and projects nanoMuse were released on Hugging Face Papers, providing a peer-to-peer implementation of Meta Muse open source under GPL-3.0: users have an agent on their mobile phones, computers and web pages, sharing the same session and connected through a self-hosted relay; each action is approved by the Sentinel scope, the memory is saved in a human-readable Markdown file, and the underlying model can be selected. The report also uses five questions and three time scales to define "personal intelligence", and describes how Muse is built based on Meta's public information and its production prompt word copy.
items.comment: It is worth noting that in addition to commercial personal assistants, there are open source routes that emphasize self-hosting and memory-readability.

items.title: Paper UniWAM: Unified World-Action Model
items.summary: The paper proposes UniWAM, which integrates the physical reasoner, world generator and action predictor into a unified architecture to jointly learn semantic understanding, visual generation and action prediction of the physical world. The author built a cleaning and annotation pipeline for human first-view data and robot data, expressing low-level actions as natural language, and used future visual noise enhancement and historical condition flow matching to reduce the number of denoising steps in post-training. The paper claims that it has achieved SOTA in distribution performance, robustness, generalization, instruction following and long-range tasks, and reports the log-linear scaling law of human-machine collaborative training.
items.comment: It is a preprint result, and conclusions such as SOTA and scaling rules still need to be verified by peers and reproduced by third parties.

items.title: Thesis WorldSonus: Real-time synthesis of spatial sound effects for world models
items.summary: The paper proposes WorldSonus, an interactive video-to-audio framework for world models: it uses a streaming causal autoregressive diffusion architecture to synthesize audio chunks with a real-time factor of 0.41. It supports dynamic editing of sound events during the generation process through an audio-centric annotation pipeline and chunk prompt scheduling, and uses stereo and ambisonic data to achieve spatial sound effects aligned with scene geometry and camera motion. The paper claims that it reaches or exceeds the performance of the bidirectional model on the open-domain video-to-audio benchmark.
items.comment: It is a preprint readme result, and the real-time factors and alignment quality still need to be independently evaluated.

items.title: Anthropic commits $150 million over three years to support U.S. Genesis Mission
items.summary: Anthropic announced that it will invest US$150 million in the next three years to support the U.S. federal scientific research program Genesis Mission, provide Claude to more than 15 participating institutions including NASA, NIH, and NSF, and provide Claude, Claude Code and API credits for hundreds of research projects, focusing on fusion energy and quantum computing, while providing training, onboarding, and technical support to relevant scientists. The commitment was announced at the Science: A New Golden Age summit hosted by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy.
items.comment: It is worth noting that cutting-edge model companies are being embedded in national scientific research plans in the form of “scientific research infrastructure”.

items.title: Anthropic launches Cyber Mission to focus on critical infrastructure and open source security
items.summary: Anthropic launched its long-term plan Cyber Mission, with the first batch focusing on two directions: in terms of critical infrastructure, the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program was established to provide cutting-edge models, field engineers and threat research for defenders of operational technology (OT) environments such as power grids, water systems, transportation, etc.; in terms of open source software, OSS Scanner was launched to provide open source projects with regular free security scans of its strongest models. The company said it this week integrated Project Glasswing into its expanded Cyber Verification Program.
items.comment: "Using cutting-edge models for defense" may be promoted to become a routine tool, but the actual efficiency of vulnerability verification, prioritization and repair still needs to be observed.

items.title: OpenAI says it disrupted two AI-driven 'disguised identity' influence operations
items.summary: OpenAI issued an announcement saying it had disrupted two AI-powered influence operations that used fake journalist identities and a think tank to spread geopolitical information. The summary of the announcement did not disclose more details such as the subjects involved and the size of the accounts.
items.comment: Public details are limited, but it is worth noting the trend of generative AI being used to falsify the source and identity of information.

items.title: OpenAI customer case: Pollo AI uses GPT-5.6 and GPT-Image-2.5 to generate advertising creatives
items.summary: OpenAI released a customer case stating that Pollo AI combines GPT-5.6, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-Image-2.5 to help creators transform creative ideas into detailed images and cinematic video ads.
items.comment: This is a manufacturer customer case. The effect description comes from both parties and has not been independently verified.

items.title: OpenAI Case: LegalOn says Codex average daily cost dropped by 65%
items.summary: OpenAI released a case report stating that legal technology company LegalOn reduced Codex's daily estimated costs by 65% while maintaining development speed by matching models such as Astra, Sol, and Luna to specific tasks and strategically managing budgets.
items.comment: Cost figures are from vendor cases, actual benefits may vary depending on team workflow and task structure.

items.title: Manus parent company raises over US$500 million, its first round since deal with Meta fell through
items.summary: According to TechCrunch, Butterfly Effect, the parent company of Chinese AI company Manus, announced the completion of more than US$500 million in financing, led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital, with participation from existing shareholders Tencent, HSG (formerly Sequoia China), Zhen Fund, etc. This is Meta's first round of funding since it was forced to cancel a $2 billion acquisition; the company has not disclosed a valuation, and it was previously reported that it was seeking $500 million at a $4 billion valuation and was considering a Hong Kong listing. Manus recently released Manus 2.0 and the Cue application that provides email, phone and digital wallet for agents.
items.comment: It is worth noting that after mergers and acquisitions were blocked, Chinese AI application companies are returning to independent financing and potential listings.

items.title: Nous Research confirms $1.5 billion valuation, launches enterprise-focused intelligence
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Nous Research, the developer of the open source Hermes Agent, completed a US$90 million Series B round at a valuation of US$1.5 billion, led by Robot Ventures, with participation from Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung, etc., with total financing reaching US$158 million. The company claims that Hermes Agent has been cloned more than 24 million times, accounting for approximately 2.5% of global AI token usage, and will enter the enterprise market as "Hermes for Businesses", allowing enterprises to deploy multi-step workflow intelligence agents that retain data privacy; the report quoted the Wall Street Journal as saying that its annualized revenue in mid-September was approximately US$36 million.
items.comment: The token proportion is estimated by the company's self-statement, and the revenue data comes from media reports, which should be treated with caution.

items.title: Cal AI founder’s new company Persona raises $10 million, betting on personal AI wristbands
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Zach Yadegari, the teenage co-founder of calorie tracking app Cal AI, has launched Persona, a personal AI assistant startup, which has completed $10 million in financing led by Vine Ventures, with participation from Z Fellows founder Cory Levy and Collective Global. The product plan includes a $179 wristband that does not run the model on the device, encrypts data transmission and storage, supports deletion, and requires key presses or wrist movements to wake up instead of continuous monitoring; the company says it has built-in anti-phishing and anti-tip injection measures, and payment requires user confirmation and is completed through external channels such as Stripe Link. The wristband is expected to be available in December and is currently available in a free beta with a business model that includes advertising.
items.comment: What is worth paying attention to is whether its privacy proposition of "non-persistent monitoring + cloud model" can be established in actual use and auditing.

items.title: AI data center company Firmus slashes valuation before listing, may put IPO on hold
items.summary: AI data center company Firmus Technologies has slashed its valuation ahead of an expected ASX listing and may even put the IPO on hold, according to Guardian Australia. According to people familiar with the matter, its valuation has risen from US$1.85 billion to about US$15 billion in more than a year, and has recently approached US$44 billion. It is currently being repriced due to insufficient investor support; the company has only two small operating sites, and about 97% of its contracted revenue comes from sites that have not yet been built. Its investors include Nvidia, Blackstone, Jane Street and Coatue. The company has also temporarily withdrawn from attending the parliamentary AI inquiry.
items.comment: Possibly reflecting valuation and delivery schedule risks amid the AI infrastructure boom, the final issuance outcome remains uncertain.

items.title: Google launches local-first meeting note-taking app AI Edge Foresight
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Google has released Google AI Edge Foresight, a Mac-side meeting note-taking application that can run completely offline and uses a terminal-side EmbeddingGemma 2 model with approximately 740 million parameters to complete transcription and note-taking. The interface is similar to Granola, supporting handwriting shorthand on the left and AI-generated notes on the right. You can also use the Gemma 4-driven assistant to ask questions about notes and uploaded documents (PDF, Google Docs, Office files, Markdown, web bookmarks, etc.). The official FAQ says the app is optimized for Apple Silicon.
items.comment: It is worth noting that highly sensitive scenarios such as meeting records are becoming a testing ground for end-side models.

items.title: Meta’s Muse launches iPad version, expands connectors and retail partners
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Meta’s AI assistant Muse launched an iPad version about a month after it was launched on the iPhone. According to Sensor Tower, the cumulative number of installations has exceeded 6.6 million. Muse can connect user accounts to handle emails, meetings, bills and other matters, and complete reservations, shopping and other operations on behalf of users; this update adds connectors and Meta advertising account support for Asana, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Klaviyo, Zoom, Notion, Granola, etc., and expands retail partners such as Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart, Wayfair, etc. The report also mentioned the problem of websites misidentifying agents as robots and blocking them. Meta is working with industry partners to promote open standards that allow agents to self-report their identities.
items.comment: It is worth noting that the friction between agent operation and website anti-bot mechanisms is becoming a real problem that requires standards coordination.

items.title: British Co-op legal department was exposed to use AI to monitor and score employee calls
items.summary: The Guardian reported that Co-op Legal Services, a subsidiary of British Co-op, uses automatic listening technology to record, analyze and give a percentage score to each call between employees and clients. It is said that OpenAI’s model evaluates more than 50 indicators in the call and provides pass/fail results to managers. It is mainly used in wills and estate consulting business and to help improve sales performance. An anonymous whistleblower employee called the system "oppressive and dystopian" and said he could be monitored by AI for hours a day; Co-op responded that the tool was only used for quality assurance and supporting colleagues, and was not involved in decision-making. Unions have begun to push back against AI surveillance in the workplace.
items.comment: It is worth noting that workplace AI surveillance is becoming a new focus in industrial relations and supervision.

items.title: Australian media: OpenAI’s email notifying the Australian government was partly written by AI
items.summary: Guardian Australia exclusively reported that some of the wording and formatting of the email used by OpenAI to notify the Australian government that its AI agents had accessed Services Australia data were generated by the company's legal and security teams using AI, but people familiar with the matter said the final email was manually reviewed and sent manually. When asked about the matter at a parliamentary hearing, OpenAI executives said they did not believe their own technology was used to write the email. The incident involved a June 18 system access and a Sept. 10 email notification, with the executive admitting that the company's "response was not good enough and should have informed affected parties earlier."
items.comment: The details are more sensitive, and what deserves attention is the reporting process of major security incidents and the transparency of technical compliance.

items.title: Australia's One Nation broadcasts AI-generated campaign videos, and supervision is accused of being unable to respond
items.summary: The Guardian reports that Australia’s One Nation played an AI-generated campaign video containing multi-ethnic stereotypes at a campaign launch in Victoria state. The article pointed out that since the video is currently only circulated online, the authority of the Australian Communications and Media Authority cannot cover such content, and the Electoral Commission can only regulate misinformation related to the election process, and the federal Labor government has so far rejected calls to ban AI-generated content during the election period.
items.comment: The author believes that existing regulatory tools are insufficient to deal with the political content of AI, and the direction of relevant legislation remains to be seen.

items.title: Investigation: Kenyan refugees work for AI outsourcing, with opaque pay and shrinking jobs
items.summary: An investigation by The Guardian reported that refugees in Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya are engaged in translation, content review, data annotation and other work for AI and data outsourcing projects, and their income is not guaranteed: some projects only provide "discretionary rewards" of up to $500 instead of guaranteed wages, and most people's income is far below the upper limit and they do not know the reason; interviewees also said that entry-level technology jobs are being reduced because of AI. In the report, AOP Connect, a platform owned by RWS, responded that the reward structure and nature of the work had been transparently informed in advance, and that the platform was not used for AI model training.
items.comment: What deserves attention is the issue of remuneration transparency and bargaining power of workers at the bottom of the AI data supply chain.

items.title: Common Sense Media rates "ChatGPT for Teens" as an unacceptable risk
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Common Sense Media, a non-profit organization, released a review and rated OpenAI's "ChatGPT for Teens" as "unacceptable risk", saying that its wording to encourage continued dialogue "remains common in crisis situations" and did not identify the risk of teenagers forming unhealthy relationships with the chatbot itself. It failed to meet the standards for three of the five serious harms, saying that some protections (such as refusal of sexual role-playing) were effective and others did not fulfill their promises. OpenAI countered that the testing method did not accurately reflect the actual operation of its youth protection mechanism, and questioned that the testing may have begun before the parental control feature was fully effective.
items.comment: The conclusions of both parties are controversial. What is worth paying attention to is the difference between the safety standards for teenagers' AI use and the evaluation methods themselves.

items.title: First U.S. sentencing in AI-assisted streaming fraud case: 18 months in prison and forfeiture of approximately $8.09 million
items.summary: Ars Technica reported that the U.S. Department of Justice said that 54-year-old Michael Smith of North Carolina used AI to generate songs, cooperated with tens of thousands of bots and hundreds of thousands of fake accounts, and boosted sales on Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify, YouTube Music and other platforms. He was sentenced to 18 months in prison and forfeited $8,091,843.64. The Department of Justice said this was the first criminal prosecution in the United States for AI-assisted streaming fraud. The prosecutor said that in one of the cases, its fake songs were played 80.9 million times in April 2023, while Taylor Swift’s entire catalog was played 9.3 million times in the same period; the defendant’s lawyer had argued that one person should not be responsible for industry problems.
items.comment: It is worth noting that generative AI is amplifying the risk of fraud in copyright revenue distribution and platform economy.

items.title: Developers use Claude Opus 5.5 to build seven open source alternatives to Adobe software
items.summary: Ars Technica reports that developer Brandon Thomas has used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 to build seven "clean room" open source alternatives to Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign and Acrobat Pro in Rust (with a WebAssembly version available), a move his Artcraft brand announced last week. The project is currently in "ultra-early alpha". The author first said that 100% functional equivalence would be achieved within a month, but later changed his statement on Hacker News and said that 99% would require "months" of time; the software is provided for free under the MIT/Apache license and relies on token access income from the Artcraft visual AI model and IDE to maintain development. The article also reminds that if its interface is imitated excessively, it may face legal risks such as "trade dress".
items.comment: What deserves attention is the open source replica model spawned by AI-assisted reverse engineering, and its tension with the boundaries of intellectual property.

items.title: WIRED: Engineers let GPT-6 Astra drive to buy burgers
items.summary: WIRED reported that three AI engineers from the startup Axiom connected OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to a set of windshield cameras and vehicle steering systems, and let this universal language model drive a 2024 Toyota Corolla to the drive-thru window of In-N-Out to pick up food. A safety driver was on standby with his foot on the brake throughout the entire process, and no pre-training was done for the driving task. The report also mentioned that Scale AI and Elorian AI launched a benchmark called "Humanity's Sixth Sense" to measure the model's ability to understand physical scenes, and that some researchers left large companies to establish start-up companies focusing on physical reasoning.
items.comment: The author believes that the language model has a preliminary understanding of the physical world, but applying the general model to driving is still a high-risk experiment and should not be regarded as a deployable autonomous driving solution.
